posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Where did the antimatter go? The Big Bang should have created equal amounts of matter and antimatter, which would have annihilated each other instantly. So why does anything exist at all? Scientists are still hunting for the missing half of reality.

What we know about human history is only a fraction of the full story. Much of the rest is like dark matter, invisible to us. We can’t see it, and we can only see the effects of its presence. But thanks to new techniques for DNA sequencing, dating ancient detritus, mathematical models, and aerial and lidar archaeology, we are now able to get a faint idea of what this world might have looked and felt like.

recentPosts.caption:
Looking for love in Ireland? You might want to find this book! 💚📖 ⁠
Meet the Irish Matchmaking Festival in Lisdoonvarna, where Willy Daly’s matchmaking book has been passed down through generations of matchmakers for around 160 years.⁠
⁠
According to local lore, touching the book’s cover for seven seconds could bring you love, or even marriage within a year. ⁠
Would you give it a try? And be honest… how many seconds would you hold on? 😂⁠
🎥: @traveltherapywithbee

Photographer @oliverhl captured a cormorant fisherman of Yangshuo, China, sitting on his bamboo raft with his trained bird by his side, surrounded by towering karst mountains.⁠
⁠
For centuries, fishermen here worked with cormorants that dive underwater to catch fish. ⁠
⁠
Today, modern fishing has mostly replaced this way of life, and only a handful of fishermen like him still keep the tradition alive.

A massage in Bangkok that feels more like a party than a spa day! 😂💆‍♀️ ⁠
BRADBURY, where a one-hour session combines 40 minutes of leg and shoulder massage with 20 minutes of dancing.⁠
⁠
The experience cost ฿8,945 (around €240) for three people, so it’s definitely a splurge rather than your usual massage. ⁠
⁠
But when relaxation meets a dance floor, you know it’s going to be an experience to remember! 💃⁠
🎥: @tsaklidi

Japan has a way of surprising you around every corner. It’s a place where centuries-old traditions sit right next to modern life, and every season paints it in a different colour. ⁠
⁠
Fair warning: these photos might send you straight to the booking page.⁠ ;)⁠
⁠
By: @llittlepig

Imagine going out for dinner and getting told off by your mum the entire time! 😂🍽️ ⁠
50’s Prime Time Café at Disney’s Hollywood Studios in Florida, is where the servers play the role of your family and the dining experience comes with a side of playful scolding.⁠
⁠
Set in a retro 1950s kitchen with vintage sitcoms playing on the TV, this restaurant combines comfort food with a nostalgic, interactive atmosphere. The service might be cheeky, but the food is a crowd-pleaser! 💛⁠
🎥: @drchristineh

This leopard is enjoying the view from an abandoned watchtower. 🐆⁠
⁠
Photographer @kritiwaliaphotography captured Bahadur, a 13-year-old leopard known as the “king of Jhalana,” sitting on an old watchtower inside Jhalana Leopard Reserve in India.⁠
⁠
The tower was once used by forest guards to spot fires and monitor the Aravalli Hills. Today, it has become a favorite vantage point for the reserve’s leopards. ⁠
⁠
Bahadur is also believed to be the father of around 75% of Jhalana’s leopard populat

⁠Boulders Beach in South Africa is home to a famous colony of African penguins. 🐧 The sheltered coves have calm water, large granite boulders, and views of the birds as they move between the rocks and sea.⁠
⁠
The colony first arrived here in 1982 and has since become one of Cape Town’s most famous attractions.

The Dragon Blood Tree, a natural wonder that looks like something from another planet.⁠
Native to Yemen’s Socotra Archipelago, this extraordinary tree releases a deep-red resin when its bark is cut or damaged, giving it its mysterious name. ⁠
⁠
Its unique umbrella-shaped canopy helps it survive in Socotra’s harsh, dry climate by capturing moisture from the air.⁠
Some of these remarkable trees are believed to live for centuries, although their exact lifespan remains uncertain. ⁠
🎥: @thisisranatr

Inside Hotel Monteleone in New Orleans’ French Quarter, the Carousel Bar has been slowly turning since 1949. Its 25 seats make one full rotation every 15 minutes, so guests see the room change while they sip.⁠
⁠
The hotel has welcomed literary legends like Ernest Hemingway, Tennessee Williams, and Truman Capote. ⁠
⁠
By: @hotelmonteleone

What does a drink for just $0.20 taste like? 👀⁠
You’ll find surprises like this on the streets of Bangladesh! ⁠
⁠
Would you dare to give it a try?⁠
🎥: @hugh.abroad

Some faces tell a whole life story without saying a word 🤍⁠
⁠
Photographer @nattysingh captures the people behind those stories: a lifetime of sun, sorrow, laughter, and love, written into every line.⁠
⁠
Beyond what we see, there’s a universe of memories, journeys, and experiences that shape who we are, and who we become. ⁠
⁠
In his own words: “One day, if we are lucky, life will write its story across our faces too… of all we loved, all we lost, and everything we somehow survived”.⁠

This canyon looks like it doesn’t belong on Earth. ⁠
⁠
Socotra, Yemen, is known for some of the most unique nature you’ll find anywhere in the world. Strange, unique trees, white limestone cliffs, turquoise water, and dry valleys all come together across the island.⁠
⁠
It’s the kind of place where every view seems completely different from the last.⁠
⁠
By: @primpaul
